record.context_brief: maximal rank for realizations with given symmetry type
record.original_question: Fix Euclidean space E^d. For each symmetry type graph T, determine the largest rank n for which there exist finite n-polytopes, and separately infinite n-polytopes, admitting a faithful symmetric realization in E^d with symmetry type graph T.

evidence.quote: Problem 22. For each symmetry type graph T, determine the maximum n such that finite (or infinite) n-polytopes admit a faithful symmetric realization in E^d with symmetry type graph T.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ be a fixed integer, and let $\mathbb{E}^d$ denote Euclidean $d$-space with isometry group $\mathrm{Iso}(\mathbb{E}^d)$. An abstract $n$-polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is a ranked partially ordered set (with ranks $-1,0,1,\dots,n$) whose elements (called faces) satisfy the standard combinatorial axioms for abstract polytopes: it has a unique least face and unique greatest face, every maximal chain (flag) has exactly $n+2$ elements, $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (every section of rank $1$ has exactly two faces of the intermediate rank). The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts on the set of flags, and the symmetry type graph $T(\mathcal{P},\Gamma)$ of $\mathcal{P}$ under a subgroup $\Gamma\le\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ is the edge-labeled multigraph (with labels in $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$) whose vertices are the orbits of $\Gamma$ on flags and whose $i$-labeled edges record the $i$-adjacency of flags between orbits.

A realization of $\mathcal{P}$ in $\mathbb{E}^d$ is a mapping $\beta$ from the vertex set of $\mathcal{P}$ to $\mathbb{E}^d$ that extends recursively to all faces so that each $j$-face is sent to the set of $(j-1)$-faces it contains. The realization is called faithful if $\beta$ is injective on the faces of each rank, and symmetric if every automorphism in some chosen subgroup $\Gamma\le\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ is induced by an isometry of $\mathbb{E}^d$; in that case the symmetry type graph of the realization is defined to be $T(\mathcal{P},\Gamma)$.

Problem. Given $d$ and an admissible edge-labeled multigraph $T$ (with edge labels in $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ for some $n$), determine:

(a) the largest integer $n$ for which there exists a finite abstract $n$-polytope admitting a faithful symmetric realization in $\mathbb{E}^d$ whose symmetry type graph equals $T$;

(b) the largest integer $n$ for which there exists an infinite abstract $n$-polytope admitting a faithful symmetric realization in $\mathbb{E}^d$ whose symmetry type graph equals $T$.
artifact.status_search_result: No evidence was found that this problem has been resolved. It is posed as an open problem on $k$-orbit polytopes, and no subsequent literature appears to give a complete answer for arbitrary symmetry type graphs $T$ and ambient dimension $d$.
